title: The identity inclusion induces the identity transition.
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme, let $\ell$ be a prime, and fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ use its ring of integers $O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $O_{E,X}$ and $E_X$ for the pulled-back coefficient rings [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] of the continuous-function condensed rings $\underline{O}_E$ [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring] and $\underline E$ [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring], with the topologies restricted from $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For $n\geq0$ put $B_{E,n}=O_E/(\ell^{n+1})$, give this finite ring the discrete topology, and denote by $B_{E,n,X}$ the pullback of its continuous-function condensed ring [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Let $r_{E,n}:O_{E,X}\to B_{E,n,X}$ be the coefficient change [def-sfb-coefficient-map] of postcomposition with the quotient map [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], and $c_E:O_{E,X}\to E_X$ the pulled-back inclusion [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield]. Write $\mu_n=\mu_{\ell^{n+1},X}$ [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Form the $O_{E,X}$-module $L_E=\varprojlim_{n\geq0}(B_{E,n,X}\otimes_{\mathbf Z_X}\mu_n)$, restricting scalars along $r_{E,n}$; the adjacent maps are quotient on $B$ and $u\mapsto u^\ell$ on roots [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Denote its underlying abelian-sheaf projections by $p_{E,n}$. Put $T_E=E_X\otimes_{O_{E,X}}L_E$, the extension of scalars of $L_E$ along $c_E$ [def-sfb-modobj-extension], and let $q_E:E_X\otimes_{\mathbf Z_X}L_E\to T_E$ be its defining coequalizer projection.

For an inclusion $h:E\subseteq F$, let $i_h:E_X\to F_X$ be its pulled-back coefficient map [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map]. Use the uniquely characterized maps $a_h:O_{E,X}\to O_{F,X}$ with $c_Fa_h=i_hc_E$ [lem-route-sp-integers-map-exists-unique], $b_{h,n}:B_{E,n,X}\to B_{F,n,X}$ with $b_{h,n}r_{E,n}=r_{F,n}a_h$ [lem-route-sp-ell-map-exists-unique], $g_h:L_E\to L_F$ with $p_{F,n}g_h=(b_{h,n}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mu_n})p_{E,n}$ [lem-route-sp-integral-twist-map-exists-unique], and $j_h:T_E\to T_F$ with $j_hq_E=q_F(i_h\otimes g_h)$ [lem-route-sp-rational-twist-map-exists-unique]. Composites in these formulas are written in functional order; $a_h$ is a morphism of ring objects and the other displayed twist maps are underlying abelian-sheaf maps. Then the rational transition of the identity inclusion is the identity: $j_{E\subseteq E}=\mathrm{id}_{T_E}$. Equivalently, $\operatorname{spRationalTwistMap}(X,\ell,\mathrm{le\_refl}(E))=\mathrm{id}$.

proof.text: For $h:E\subseteq E$ the condensed inclusion is postcomposition with the identity, hence is the identity by [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map]. Its image under $p_X^*$ is the identity by the functor identity axiom and [def-sfb-coefficient-map]; thus $i_h=\mathrm{id}_{E_X}$. In the characterization of [lem-route-sp-integers-map-exists-unique], $\mathrm{id}_{O_{E,X}}$ preserves unit and multiplication and satisfies $c_E\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}\,c_E$. Uniqueness gives $a_h=\mathrm{id}_{O_{E,X}}$.

proof.text: For every $n\geq0$, [lem-route-sp-ell-map-exists-unique] characterizes $b_{h,n}$ by $b_{h,n}r_{E,n}=r_{E,n}a_h$. Since step 1 gives $a_h=\mathrm{id}$, the identity of $B_{E,n,X}$ satisfies this equation: both sides are $r_{E,n}$. Its uniqueness gives $b_{h,n}=\mathrm{id}_{B_{E,n,X}}$.

source.place: Integral inverse-limit and rationalization paragraph, field-extension diagram implicit in the colimit over E; explicit identity-normalization argument in lean/Sheaf/Paper/ProEtaleTateTwists.lean, spRationalTwistMap_id docstring and preceding four uniqueness declarations (lines 268–362).

proof.text: By [lem-route-sp-integral-twist-map-exists-unique], $g_h$ is the unique abelian-sheaf map whose composites with $p_{E,n}$ are $(b_{h,n}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mu_n})p_{E,n}$. Step 2 makes each right side $p_{E,n}$, since tensoring two identity maps is the identity (the tensor bifunctor identity axiom). The identity of $L_E$ has exactly these composites. Uniqueness gives $g_h=\mathrm{id}_{L_E}$.

source.place: Integral inverse-limit and rationalization paragraph, field-extension diagram implicit in the colimit over E; explicit identity-normalization argument in lean/Sheaf/Paper/ProEtaleTateTwists.lean, spRationalTwistMap_id docstring and preceding four uniqueness declarations (lines 268–362).

proof.text: By [lem-route-sp-rational-twist-map-exists-unique], $j_h$ is the unique abelian-sheaf map with $j_hq_E=q_E(i_h\otimes g_h)$. Steps 1 and 3 make the right side $q_E(\mathrm{id}\otimes\mathrm{id})=q_E$. The identity of $T_E$ satisfies the same equation, since $\mathrm{id}\,q_E=q_E$. Uniqueness therefore gives $j_h=\mathrm{id}_{T_E}$, as required.
